lab_title: Vectors and 2D Projectile Motion in AR
top_level_objectives: Understand vectors as mathematical entities with both magnitude and direction.
Perform graphical vector addition using the tip-to-tail method.
Decompose vectors into horizontal and vertical components using right-triangle trigonometry.
Apply vector decomposition to projectile motion to understand the independence of horizontal and vertical velocities.
Analyze how changing the initial velocity and launch angle affects a projectile's trajectory, maximum height, and range.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of vectors as mathematical objects possessing both magnitude and direction.
key_visuals: A 3D cartesian coordinate grid floating in the AR space.
A large, interactive glowing arrow representing a vector.
Floating text panels displaying the vector's current magnitude and angle relative to the x-axis.
student_actions: Grab the tip of the vector to stretch it (changing magnitude) and rotate it (changing direction).
Observe how the numerical values on the text panels update in real-time as the vector is manipulated.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate graphical vector addition to find a resultant vector.
key_visuals: Two distinct vectors (Vector A in blue, Vector B in red) originating from the same point.
A dashed resultant vector (Vector C in purple).
student_actions: Drag Vector B so that its tail connects to the tip of Vector A.
Watch the resultant vector automatically draw itself from the tail of Vector A to the new position of Vector B's tip.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how a single vector can be decomposed into horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components using right-triangle trigonometry.
key_visuals: A main vector on a grid with a right-triangle overlay.
Secondary arrows representing the x and y components of the vector.
Mathematical labels showing 'V*cos(θ)' for the x-component and 'V*sin(θ)' for the y-component.
student_actions: Toggle a button to reveal or hide the x and y component vectors.
Change the angle of the main vector and observe how the lengths of the orthogonal components change, noting when one becomes zero.

scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector concepts to a physical scenario by setting the initial velocity of a projectile.
key_visuals: A 3D cannon or launcher positioned on a tabletop or floor.
A spherical projectile loaded in the cannon.
An initial velocity vector attached to the projectile, which can be decomposed into horizontal and vertical components.
student_actions: Adjust the initial launch angle and speed by manipulating the initial velocity vector.
Press a 'Launch' button to fire the projectile and watch it follow a parabolic path.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate the independence of horizontal and vertical motion during the projectile's flight.
key_visuals: The projectile moving along its parabolic trajectory.
Dynamic vectors attached to the projectile during flight: a constant horizontal velocity arrow (Vx) and a changing vertical velocity arrow (Vy).
student_actions: Use a time-scrubbing slider to move the projectile forward and backward through its flight path.
Observe that the horizontal vector (Vx) never changes length, while the vertical vector (Vy) shrinks to zero at the peak and points downward, growing larger as it falls.

scenes.brief_purpose: Experiment with launch parameters to understand their effects on trajectory, range, and maximum height.
key_visuals: The launcher setup with a target area placed at a distance.
AR measuring tapes showing the total horizontal range and the maximum vertical height achieved.
Faded 'ghost' trails of previous launches for comparison.
student_actions: Systematically change the launch angle (from 0 to 90 degrees) while keeping speed constant to discover the angle for maximum range (45 degrees).
Adjust both speed and angle to successfully hit targets placed at varying distances and heights.
